input_analysis: login-homepage-v2 is a fresh single-phase standard-chain pilot. The repository already has historical examples under examples/login_homepage_app and examples/feedback_thanks_app plus tests, but the new run must use new implementation, test, and evidence anchors. Code scan found no product web framework to extend, so an isolated Python standard-library HTTP example preserves the existing pilot style and avoids dependency noise. docs/constitution.md is absent, so no project-level constitution constraints are inherited into this design.
key_decisions: Implement a new isolated Python standard-library HTTP app under examples/login_homepage_v2_app instead of modifying historical pilot code.
Model one configured account loaded from environment variables, with server-side in-memory sessions and an HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie.
Exercise acceptance through real local HTTP tests in tests/test_login_homepage_v2_app.py.
Keep role-capability and noise-control evidence as a dedicated support artifact referenced by delivery evidence, while canonical gates remain the standard-chain JSON artifacts.

option_analysis.summary: Create a new isolated Python standard-library HTTP app and tests for login-homepage-v2.
option_analysis.tradeoff: Matches current repository pilot patterns, adds no dependency stack, and makes fresh evidence easy to separate from historical pilots.

option_analysis.summary: Modify or wrap the existing examples/login_homepage_app implementation.
option_analysis.tradeoff: Reduces code volume but weakens the core requirement that this run proves a fresh from-scratch demand loop.

option_analysis.summary: Introduce a web framework such as Flask or FastAPI for the sample app.
option_analysis.tradeoff: Could look closer to production web development but introduces unrelated dependency and setup noise for a process-readiness pilot.

runtime_facts: Command `rg --files examples tests docs | rg 'login_homepage|login-homepage|feedback_thanks|feedback-thanks'` found historical pilot artifacts and no existing login-homepage-v2 implementation.

Command `wc -l examples/login_homepage_app/app.py examples/feedback_thanks_app/app.py tests/test_login_homepage_app.py tests/test_feedback_thanks_app.py` showed comparable pilot files are below the 400-line repository file limit.

Runtime capture for deployed services is not applicable: this feature adds only a local example app and local tests, with no production process, external service, database, config center, or port allocation.
Credentials are injected through test-owned environment variables or an explicit LoginConfig object; no business secret is stored in the repository.

interfaces.contract_summary: GET /login returns a 200 HTML login form with username and password inputs and optional escaped error content.
POST /login parses a bounded URL-encoded body, validates the configured account, creates a server-side session on success, and renders a readable error on failure.
output_params: success: 303 Location / plus Set-Cookie session token
failure: 401 login HTML with role=alert and no Set-Cookie

interfaces.contract_summary: GET / protects the homepage with the server-side session map and renders the escaped configured identity plus welcome content only for valid sessions.
output_params: valid session: 200 HTML homepage with identity, welcome content, and logout action

interfaces.contract_summary: POST /logout removes the current server-side session and returns an expired session cookie before redirecting to /login.
error_modes: missing or unknown session still returns a safe login redirect

interfaces.contract_summary: Support evidence records each standard-chain role input, output, responsibility boundary, downstream consumer, and noise-control result for this run.
error_modes: old pilot evidence used as completion proof

migration_plan: Add new v2 implementation and tests without modifying historical login-homepage-pilot code.
Keep old pilot artifacts available only as repository pattern references, not as acceptance evidence.
Register or reference new v2 artifacts through the v2 artifact registry during delivery.
verification_plan: Run RED acceptance tests before implementation to prove the new v2 path is not already satisfied.
Run GREEN acceptance tests through a real local ThreadingHTTPServer after implementation.
Run standard-chain phase validation for docs/login-homepage-v2/phase-1 after each artifact layer is added.
Run readiness and replay validation after review, QA, consistency, signoff, artifact registry, and user decision artifacts exist.
Run a path isolation check that rejects using docs/login-homepage-pilot or tests/test_login_homepage_app.py as v2 completion evidence.
rollback_plan: Remove the new examples/login_homepage_v2_app package and tests/test_login_homepage_v2_app.py if implementation validation fails and cannot be repaired inside scope.
Quarantine unfinished docs/login-homepage-v2 artifacts instead of mixing them into historical pilot evidence.
Preserve existing login-homepage-pilot and feedback-thanks-pilot artifacts unchanged.
